title: Light Bends Around the Abyss
narration: This black hole wears a halo of stolen light. Its gravity is so fierce it bends the glow from the disk behind it into a perfect ring, while a torrent of superheated gas spins around the edge of forever. Nothing that crosses that boundary ever returns.

title: Two Giants Dance to the End
narration: Two monster black holes are locked in a death spiral. One holds two hundred million times the mass of the Sun, the other half that, each warping the other's glowing gas into impossible shapes. Soon they merge, shaking the very fabric of spacetime.

title: The Strongest Magnet in Existence
narration: Meet the most magnetic object known to science. A single teaspoon of this neutron star would weigh billions of tons, and its magnetic field could wipe a credit card from halfway to the Moon. In twenty twenty it screamed a radio burst across our galaxy.

title: A Lighthouse of the Cosmos
narration: Spinning hundreds of times a second, this dead star sweeps beams of radiation across the universe like a cosmic lighthouse. Each flash reaches us with clockwork precision so exact it rivals atomic clocks. A city-sized corpse, keeping perfect time forever.

title: Brighter Than a Trillion Suns
narration: Aimed straight at us is the brightest engine in the universe. A supermassive black hole gorges on swirling gas and fires a jet of particles at nearly light speed, outshining its entire galaxy of billions of stars. We are staring down the barrel.

title: A Star Torn Into Spaghetti
narration: Watch a whole star stretched into a noodle of fire. When it wanders too close, a black hole a million times the Sun's mass rips it apart, shredding it into a long glowing stream of gas. Astronomers call this spaghettification, and it is terrifyingly real.

title: The Universe's Deadliest Blast
narration: In mere seconds, this explosion releases more energy than the Sun will in its entire ten-billion-year life. A dying giant star collapses and fires a jet of gamma rays across the cosmos, leaving a fading afterglow. It is the most violent event we know.

title: A Dead Sun Devours Worlds
narration: Here glows the ember of a star like our Sun, crushed to the size of Earth. So dense that a sugar cube of it would weigh a ton, this white dwarf now tears apart and swallows a rocky world. Even in death, it feeds.

title: Andromeda Is Coming for Us
narration: Our galaxy is on a collision course. In a few billion years the Milky Way and Andromeda will crash together, their billions of stars sweeping past each other without a single impact, before merging into one giant elliptical. The night sky will never look the same.

title: Every Galaxy on Invisible Threads
narration: The universe has a hidden skeleton. Galaxies hang like beads of light along vast purple filaments of dark matter, stretching across hundreds of millions of light-years. This cosmic web links everything that exists, woven by gravity since the dawn of time. We live inside it.

title: Mapping a Billion Stars
narration: Behold our galaxy drawn from nearly two billion stars. The Gaia spacecraft measured each one's exact position, brightness, and color, building the most precise map of the Milky Way ever made. Sweep from Cassiopeia to Orion through a sky charted star by star.

title: Watch Planets Being Born
narration: Two glowing spiral arms are carving through this disk of gas and dust around a young star. Hidden inside those swirls, brand-new planets may be sculpting the material as they form. You are witnessing the very birth of worlds, four hundred light-years away.

title: How We Find Hidden Worlds
narration: A tiny dip in starlight just revealed an alien planet. As a distant world crosses its star, it blocks a sliver of light, and that faint flicker is how Kepler and TESS have found thousands of exoplanets. We hunt new worlds by watching shadows.

title: Seven Earths Around One Star
narration: Around one tiny dwarf star spin seven Earth-sized worlds, several in the zone where liquid water could exist. Stand on one and the neighboring planets would loom larger than our Moon. Forty light-years away, this could be the best place to search for life.

title: A Planet Hotter Than Stars
narration: This gas giant skims so close to its star that its dayside hits over four thousand degrees, hotter than many stars themselves. Three times the mass of Jupiter, it is boiling away into space, its atmosphere streaming off like steam. A world cooked slowly alive.

title: The Corpse of an Exploded Star
narration: Almost a thousand years ago, Chinese astronomers watched this star explode in broad daylight. Today its glowing wreckage spreads across light-years, lit up from radio waves to X-rays, with a spinning pulsar at its heart. This is what a star leaves behind when it dies violently.

title: Towers Where Stars Are Born
narration: These towering pillars of gas stand taller than our entire solar system. Deep inside the cold columns, gravity crushes matter together until brand-new stars ignite. Hubble and Webb peered into the same nursery to watch fresh starlight breaking out of the darkness.

title: A Canyon to Swallow Continents
narration: Soar over the largest canyon in the solar system. Valles Marineris slices across Mars for over two thousand miles, deep enough to swallow Earth's Grand Canyon many times over. Carved into the red planet, this scar would stretch clear across the United States.

title: Diving Into Jupiter's Storms
narration: Plunge to just two thousand miles above Jupiter's clouds. The Juno spacecraft captured these swirling bands and monster vortices, storms wider than entire planets churning across the largest world in our solar system. Down here the chaos never ends, and it never has.

title: The Crown of the Solar System
narration: Saturn's rings span tens of thousands of miles, yet are mostly just yards thick, built from countless chunks of ice. Cassini orbited here for thirteen years before its final, fiery plunge into the planet. These real images are its parting gift to us.

title: An Ocean Under Cracked Ice
narration: Beneath this shattered shell of ice hides a global ocean holding twice the water of all Earth's seas. The cracks reveal where warm currents churn the surface into chaos. On this moon of Jupiter, deep dark water may be our best place to search for life.

title: Rivers of Liquid Methane
narration: On Saturn's largest moon it rains, but not water. Under a thick orange haze, methane falls from the clouds, carving rivers and filling vast seas with liquid fuel. Titan is the only other world we know with stable lakes on its surface. A frigid, alien Earth.

title: A Moon That Sprays the Sky
narration: This little moon shoots fountains of ocean water straight into space. From cracks called tiger stripes, geysers blast ice, vapor, and organic chemicals hundreds of miles high, fed by a hidden sea below. Enceladus is quite literally leaking the ingredients for life.

title: The Most Volcanic World
narration: Painted in sulfur yellows and reds, this moon is the most volcanic place in the solar system. Hundreds of erupting peaks fling plumes high above the surface as Jupiter's gravity flexes and heats its insides. Io is a tortured world that never stops erupting.

title: Pluto's Frozen Heart
narration: Glide over mountains made of water ice, hard as rock in the deep cold. Below them spreads a vast plain of frozen nitrogen, the left half of Pluto's famous heart. New Horizons captured this distant world in stunning detail after a nine-year journey to the edge.

title: Scorched and Battered by the Sun
narration: Closest to the Sun spins this scarred grey world. Mercury has almost no atmosphere to shield it, so its surface swings from scorching heat to deep freeze and bears the marks of countless ancient impacts. A planet hammered and baked for billions of years.

title: A Furnace That Melts Lead
narration: Welcome to the hottest planet in the solar system. Venus broils at nearly nine hundred degrees, hot enough to melt lead, beneath crushing clouds of acid. The Parker probe pierced that veil to glimpse its glowing surface in visible light for the very first time.

title: Worlds at the Cold Frontier
narration: Far out in the freezing dark drift two ice giants. Uranus rolls on its side, tipped over by an ancient collision, while Neptune whips up the fastest winds in the solar system, over a thousand miles an hour. Hubble keeps watch on these distant blue worlds.

title: Touching an Asteroid to Steal Dust
narration: A spacecraft reached out and tapped an asteroid. OSIRIS-REx descended to Bennu, pressed its arm into the rubble for just six seconds, and grabbed a sample of dust older than the planets. Then it carried that ancient cargo all the way home to Earth.

title: Leftovers From the Planets' Birth
narration: Between Mars and Jupiter drifts the wreckage of a planet that never formed. These millions of rocky asteroids are leftover rubble from our solar system's violent birth, frozen survivors of a chaotic era of collisions. Each one is a time capsule from four billion years ago.

title: When the Sun Strikes the Sky
narration: The northern lights are born from a cosmic collision. When the solar wind slams into Earth's magnetic field, snapping magnetic lines in the planet's tail unleash a burst of energy that sets the polar sky ablaze in green and red. The Sun is painting our atmosphere.

title: Racing Earth at 17,500 mph
narration: From two hundred twenty miles up, watch our planet glow. The Space Station circles Earth at seventeen thousand five hundred miles an hour, fast enough to see a sunrise every ninety minutes. City lights and a thin blue haze shine against the black of space.

title: Humanity's Farthest Traveler
narration: Follow the most distant machine humans ever built. After decades of flight, Voyager crossed the boundary where the Sun's wind fades and true interstellar space begins. Now over a hundred times farther from the Sun than Earth, it carries our message into the galaxy.

title: A Frozen Wanderer Wakes Up
narration: Watch a comet blaze to life. This frozen wanderer spent billions of years in the deep cold, until sunlight boiled its ice into a glowing tail streaming millions of miles across space. We get one fleeting show before it vanishes into the dark for a thousand years.

title: Seeing the First Galaxies
narration: Zoom into thousands of galaxies in a patch of sky smaller than your fingernail. That faint red dot ranks among the most distant galaxies ever seen, its light traveling more than thirteen billion years to reach us. James Webb is staring back to the cosmic dawn.

title: A Storm Across the Solar System
narration: The Sun just hurled a billion tons of plasma into space. This eruption races outward at over a million miles an hour, sweeping past Mars, a distant comet, and onward toward Saturn. Watch a single solar storm sail clear across the inner solar system.

title: A Dust Storm Swallows Mars
narration: On Mars, dust can grow from a local storm into a planet-wide veil. Fine red particles rise into the thin air, trap sunlight, and warm the atmosphere, helping the storm spread even farther. In twenty eighteen, one of these global storms ended the Opportunity rover's mission after fifteen years.

title: Saturn's Rings Are Falling
narration: Saturn's rings look eternal, but they are slowly raining into the planet. The rings are made mostly of countless icy fragments, from grains of dust to boulders, spread across a disk wider than Earth but often only tens of feet thick. Even the crown of the solar system is temporary.

title: An Ocean Locked Under Ice
narration: Europa hides one of the solar system's most tempting secrets. Under its cracked ice shell may lie a global ocean with more water than all of Earth's oceans combined. Jupiter's gravity flexes the moon, keeping the interior warm enough for liquid water to survive in the dark.

title: Lakes Made of Liquid Methane
narration: Titan has weather that looks strangely familiar, but the chemistry is alien. Methane and ethane rain from orange skies, flow through river channels, and collect in dark lakes near the poles. It is the only world beyond Earth known to have stable liquid on its surface.

title: A Moon Spraying Its Ocean
narration: Enceladus is small, bright, and leaking into space. From cracks near its south pole, geysers fire water vapor, ice grains, salts, and organic molecules hundreds of miles above the surface. Cassini flew through those plumes and found clues pointing to a hidden ocean below.

title: Flying Over Pluto's Heart
narration: Pluto was supposed to be a frozen, simple world. New Horizons revealed mountains of water ice, hazy blue skies, and a vast heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice slowly moving like a glacier. At the edge of the solar system, Pluto turned out to be alive with geology.

title: The Planet That Became a Furnace
narration: Venus is Earth's near twin in size, but its surface is a pressure cooker. Thick carbon dioxide air traps heat until the ground reaches about nine hundred degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt lead. Above it, clouds of sulfuric acid hide a world crushed by a runaway greenhouse effect.

title: Mercury, Scorched and Frozen
narration: Mercury lives closest to the Sun, but it is not simply a ball of heat. With almost no atmosphere, its dayside bakes while its nightside plunges into extreme cold. NASA's MESSENGER mission mapped its cratered surface and even found water ice hiding in permanently shadowed polar craters.

title: The Fastest Winds Around a Planet
narration: Neptune is the farthest major planet from the Sun, yet its atmosphere is wildly energetic. Winds can race faster than the speed of sound, pushing dark storms through deep blue clouds. Somehow this cold ice giant still powers some of the fastest weather in the solar system.

title: The Planet Knocked Sideways
narration: Uranus does not spin like the other planets. It rolls around the Sun on its side, with an axial tilt of about ninety-eight degrees, probably from a giant impact long ago. That strange lean gives it extreme seasons where each pole can face decades of sunlight, then decades of darkness.

title: A Sample From Before Earth
narration: Bennu is a rubble pile older than the planets. OSIRIS-REx touched its surface for only seconds, blasted nitrogen into the dust, and captured a sample to bring home. Inside those dark grains are chemical clues from the dawn of the solar system, before Earth had fully formed.

title: The Comet With a Lander
narration: Comet 67P looks like two icy worlds stuck together. As it nears the Sun, heat wakes the surface, jets of gas and dust burst out, and a glowing coma forms around it. Rosetta orbited this strange body for years, and Philae became the first lander to touch a comet.

title: Fossils Sharing Jupiter's Orbit
narration: Ahead of and behind Jupiter travel swarms of ancient asteroids called Trojans. They are leftovers from the chaotic time when the giant planets were settling into place. NASA's Lucy mission is visiting them because these small worlds may preserve clues about how the outer solar system was built.

title: Beyond the Sun's Bubble
narration: Voyager crossed a boundary no spacecraft had reached before. Far beyond the planets, the solar wind weakens and interstellar space begins. The probe is now traveling through material between the stars, still sending faint signals home after decades, carrying a golden record from Earth into the dark.

title: Sixteen Sunrises Every Day
narration: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly every ninety minutes. That means astronauts can see about sixteen sunrises and sunsets in a single day, watching city lights, storms, oceans, and the thin blue atmosphere slide beneath them. It is a laboratory moving faster than a rifle bullet.

title: Auroras Seen From Above
narration: From orbit, auroras are not just curtains in the sky. They form glowing rings around Earth's magnetic poles, where charged particles guided by the planet's magnetic field crash into the upper atmosphere. Oxygen and nitrogen light up in green, red, and purple, revealing our magnetic shield at work.

title: Earth's Invisible Shield
narration: Earth is wrapped in an invisible magnetic shield. The magnetosphere pushes back against the solar wind, deflecting many charged particles that would otherwise strike the atmosphere directly. It stretches into a long tail away from the Sun, turning our planet into a tiny protected bubble in space.

title: The Sun's Giant Bubble
narration: The Sun does not end at the planets. Its wind blows outward in every direction, carving a vast bubble called the heliosphere through interstellar space. Voyager crossed the edge of that bubble, showing that our entire solar system travels inside a protective shell made by the Sun.

title: A Dead Star Flashing Like a Beacon
narration: A pulsar is the crushed core of a dead star, spinning with astonishing precision. Beams of radiation stream from its magnetic poles, and if one sweeps past Earth, we see a flash. Some pulsars rotate hundreds of times every second, keeping time with cosmic accuracy.

title: A Planet With No Sunrise
narration: Some planets do not orbit any star. They drift alone through the galaxy, thrown out by gravitational chaos or born in isolation. A rogue planet would have no sunrise, no seasons, and no daylit sky, only the faint glow of distant stars above a frozen world.

title: A Million Ancient Stars
narration: Globular clusters are some of the oldest star cities in the universe. Hundreds of thousands, sometimes millions, of stars crowd into a tight sphere held together by gravity. Many formed more than ten billion years ago, long before the Sun, making them fossils of the early Milky Way.

title: The Star That Never Ignited
narration: A brown dwarf is too massive to be a planet, but too small to shine like a true star. It forms like a star from collapsing gas, then fails to sustain hydrogen fusion in its core. These dim objects glow mostly in infrared, hiding between planets and suns.

title: The Force Stretching Everything Apart
narration: The universe is not just expanding. Its expansion is speeding up. Astronomers call the mysterious driver dark energy, a name for whatever is pushing galaxies farther apart on the largest scales. We cannot see it directly, but its effect dominates the future of the cosmos.

title: How the Solar System Began
narration: Our solar system began inside a collapsing cloud of gas and dust. Most material fell into the young Sun, while the leftovers flattened into a spinning disk. Inside that disk, grains stuck together, rocks became worlds, and the planets slowly grew from cosmic dust.

title: The Frozen Ring Beyond Neptune
narration: Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt, a vast ring of icy leftovers from planet formation. Pluto is one member of this distant population, along with countless smaller bodies preserved in deep cold. Studying them is like opening a freezer full of ancient solar system material.

title: The Comet Shell Around the Sun
narration: Far beyond the planets may lie the Oort Cloud, a huge spherical reservoir of icy bodies surrounding the Sun. We have never seen it directly, but long-period comets appear to fall inward from that distant shell. It may stretch a light-year or more into space.

title: Gravity Turns Light Into a Ring
narration: A perfect ring of light can form when gravity bends the universe into a lens. If a massive galaxy lines up with a more distant galaxy behind it, spacetime curves the background light around the foreground object. The result is an Einstein ring, a prediction of relativity made visible.
